sourceAnchors.message: To be compliant to J2EE, a webapp should not use any thread.
sourceAnchors.reason: Batch CLI checks the current interrupt flag twice around the borrowed clock boundary under SS341 parent budget. These two sites create no thread or pool, do not clear a flag, and are unrelated to a J2EE web-container-managed thread prohibition.

sourceAnchors.message: Avoid catching RuntimeException in try-catch block
sourceAnchors.reason: SS332/341 SSC063/337 direct owned JDBC and transaction recovery require all unknown Runtime/Error identities to be retained, with fixed redacted secondary and original known/unknown type priority. These exact catches rethrow failure, never treat NPE as normal, and never emit provider diagnostics.

sourceAnchors.message: A throw statement in a finally block makes the control flow hard to understand.
sourceAnchors.reason: SS332/341 direct ResultSet/Statement close is once-only in these four exact finally sites. A selected unknown cleanup must supersede known SQL according to the approved matrix; values are returned only after both closes. Replacing this with generic TWR would alter the approved same-Throwable/type priority.

sourceAnchors.message: it is recommended to wrap resource 'checked' in try-with-resource declaration directly
sourceAnchors.reason: These are nonnull aliases of the exact original PreparedStatement/ResultSet already owned by the surrounding two try-with-resources declarations. No new resource is acquired by requireNonNull; the original owner closes it once on every return/throw, including null-provider contract rejection.

sourceAnchors.message: To be compliant to J2EE, a webapp should not use any thread.
sourceAnchors.reason: Independent JUnit owns this thread-state fixture and two-worker pool, not a J2EE application container. IRQ injection is always cleared in finally; all twenty independent memory-JDBC tasks have Future3 seconds and finally shutdownNow/await10 seconds. No service/native/shared connection is operated.

sourceAnchors.message: If you run in Java5 or newer and have concurrent access, you should use the ConcurrentHashMap implementation
sourceAnchors.sourceAnchor: final Map<String, Throwable> failures = new HashMap<>();
sourceAnchors.reason: Each Fixture creates its own three mutable maps and is confined to exactly one test thread or one submitted task. Twenty tasks allocate twenty distinct Fixture/Connection instances; main-thread inspection happens only after Future.get handoff. No map has concurrent access or production shared state.

sourceAnchors.message: In J2EE, getClassLoader() might not work as expected.  Use Thread.currentThread().getContextClassLoader() instead.
sourceAnchors.reason: This independent memory fixture implements only the explicit JDK Connection/PreparedStatement/ResultSet interface passed by the test. Its defining interface loader is required for typed Proxy identity; no application or native class discovery or J2EE context loader is used.
